titleEn: If It Hurts, Cry and Hug Mom!

pages.text: "This stone, that stone, hop!" Coco, in a red headscarf, hopped over alley stones. "All the way to the end without falling!" Icicles sparkled under the eaves as both of Coco's feet flew off a stone.
But the landing spot was slippery. Crash! Coco fell onto the stones. Their knee stung, and the scrape burned. Coco's mouth curved down, and their tail drooped onto the stones.
Tears welled up, but Coco held them back. "Crying makes me look like a baby mouse..." Coco pressed their lips shut. The longer Coco held it in, the tighter their throat and chest felt.
Mrs. Magpie, who saw everything from the roof, spotted Coco. She called loudly toward the bakery. "Coco's mom! Coco has fallen!" Coco sat on the stones, holding their knee.
Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, ran out. She knelt in front of Coco, face to face. "That hurt a lot, didn't it? Your closed lips keep trembling."
"You don't have to hold it in. If it hurts, cry and hug Mom!" Mom opened both floury arms wide. Coco's tightly closed mouth relaxed. "Waaah!" Coco buried their face against Mom's chest and cried.
After crying for a while, the tight feeling in Coco's chest eased. Coco peeped up, with white flour on their cheeks. Mom wiped the tears. "If it hurts, cry and hug Mom!"
Mom carried Coco into the shop. She sat Coco on a chair and patted the knee with a wet towel. Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws. "It doesn't hurt now!"
Now, when Coco hurt, they did this. "One, say it hurts! Two, cry if I want to! Three, into Mom's arms!" A few days later, Coco bumped their tail and went to Mom. "Mom, it hurts. Hug me."

Mom sat Coco on her lap and hugged them tight. When it hurts, you can cry instead of holding it in. A hug after crying soon helps the hurt feel better. Coco kissed Mom's cheek. "If it hurts, cry and hug Mom!"
